result: The crystal structure of Ecp6 reveals a novel intrachain LysM dimerization mechanism where LysM1 and LysM3 form a composite binding groove that binds a chitin tetramer (GlcNAc)4 with 12 hydrogen bonds. The structure was determined to 1.6 Å resolution and shows LysM1 separated from a compact LysM2-LysM3 body by a flexible linker.
status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly praised the structural analysis as 'excellent' and agreed that 'the publication of the ECP6 structure will be a significant contribution to the field.' No concerns were raised about the structural findings themselves, indicating reviewer acceptance of these crystallographic results.

result: The LysM1-LysM3 composite binding site mediates chitin binding with ultra-high picomolar affinity, which explains how LysM effectors outcompete plant host receptors for chitin binding.
status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly stated 'It is clear that the LysM1–3 binding site has sufficient affinity to work as the authors suggest,' indicating acceptance of the picomolar affinity measurements and their functional significance in outcompeting host receptors.

result: The singular LysM2 domain binds chitin with low micromolar affinity (Kd = 4.5 µM), approximately 1 million times lower than the LysM1-LysM3 composite site.
status_reasoning: Reviewers did not challenge the measured binding affinities for LysM2. They accepted the ITC data showing micromolar binding, though they questioned the functional interpretation of how this low affinity could suppress immunity.

result: Structure-based mutants in LysM3 (L152R and S177K) and LysM2 (T95R and D121K) were impaired in suppressing chitin-triggered immunity in tomato alkalinization assays.
status_reasoning: Reviewers requested that 'The results of the tomato protoplast assay are an important part of the manuscript' and should be better presented, and noted that 'the data supporting this in the tomato alkalinization assay are not presented' for the high-affinity site. They also requested 'statistical analysis of all the alkalinization data' and questioned whether mutants were truly non-autoactive, indicating uncertainty about the interpretation of these functional data.

result: LysM2 can suppress chitin-triggered immunity despite low micromolar affinity, possibly through interference with host immune receptor complexes rather than chitin sequestration. P. pastoris-produced Ecp6 (with only LysM2 available) suppresses immunity even though it should only sequester a small portion of chitin at the concentrations used.
status_reasoning: Reviewers raised 'A major concern' about how low affinity LysM2 could effectively suppress immunity, calculating that 'virtually none of it will be sequestered' at experimental concentrations. They stated 'the LysM2 domain does not directly out-compete for chitin-induced responses in the assay, and something else must be going on' and requested the authors 'make this conclusion stronger' that LysM2 is 'unlikely to work via sequestering chitin.' This indicates substantial uncertainty about the mechanism.

result: Chitin-free Ecp6 produced in HEK293 cells suppresses chitin-triggered immunity and shows two binding sites with different affinities in ITC experiments.
status_reasoning: Reviewers requested control ITC traces ('buffer injections into the protein, ligand injection into buffer and buffer to buffer') to demonstrate that measured heats come from interactions, and noted discrepancies with previous work ('in that paper, three binding events were documented; here it is two'). This indicates uncertainty about the ITC data interpretation and quality controls.

result: The chitin tetramer co-purified with Ecp6 from P. pastoris suggests high-affinity binding, and the structure indicates that longer chitin oligomers can bind with four GlcNAc units making direct contact while remaining parts protrude into solvent.
status_reasoning: Reviewers questioned whether the bound oligomer is actually (GlcNAc)4, asking 'Do you actually know that the chitin oligomer bound to Ecp6 purified from Pichia is (GlcNAc)4? Could it be longer? It could be possible to positively identify this by mass spectrometry.' They also noted 'It is argued that a longer GlcNAc chain could possibly bind in the same way,' indicating this remains speculative.

result: All Ecp6 mutants in LysM1 and LysM3 were able to bind chitin according to ITC analysis, though mutants in LysM3 showed reduced affinity.
status_reasoning: Reviewers asked to 'further discuss or modify the presentation of the ITC in Figure 3' and questioned 'Were the T22R and N47K data fitted to a model (indicated by the lines joining the points)? If so, what was the result?' This indicates uncertainty about the data presentation and interpretation of the mutant binding studies.

result: Mutants T22R and N47K in LysM1 resulted in autoactive proteins that triggered responses in tomato cells in the absence of chitin, though circular dichroism showed they retained proper folding.
status_reasoning: Reviewers noted 'The authors state that the L152R and S177K mutants are not autoactive, but they do show some pH shift relative to Ecp6' and requested statistical analysis, suggesting uncertainty about whether mutants are truly non-autoactive versus showing altered activity.

result: Convergent evolution has produced different structural modes for chitin binding: Ecp6 uses intrachain LysM dimerization while AtCERK1 cannot form such dimers and instead uses interchain receptor dimerization.
status_reasoning: Reviewers did not challenge the structural comparison between Ecp6 and AtCERK1 or the conclusion about convergent evolution producing different binding modes. The structural differences were accepted as part of the 'excellent structural analysis.'
